chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said:

I asked him about the zakat on raisins and dates. He said: For every five awsaq, one wasq (is the zakat), and the wasq is sixty sa'as, and the zakat on both of them is equal. But as for grain crops, the tithe (one-tenth) applies to what is irrigated by the sky (rain), and as for what is irrigated by the bucket and water-lifting devices, then only half the tithe (one-twentieth) is due.

key_terms.أَوْسَاق: Awsaq: plural of wasq, a measure of volume used for agricultural produce (1 wasq = 60 sa'as)
key_terms.التَّمْر: Dates; one of the four primary agricultural products subject to zakat in Shia fiqh
key_terms.الدَّوَالِي: Al-dawali: water-lifting devices such as pulley systems or water-wheels
key_terms.الزَّبِيب: Raisins (dried grapes); subject to zakat like fresh grapes when dried
key_terms.الْعُشْر: Al-'Ushr: the tithe, one-tenth; the standard rate for rain-irrigated crops
key_terms.الْغَرْب: Al-gharb: a large leather bucket used to draw water from wells
key_terms.صَاع: Sa': a unit of dry measure; one wasq equals sixty sa'as
key_terms.نِصْف الْعُشْر: Nisf al-'Ushr: half the tithe, i.e., one-twentieth; the reduced rate for artificially irrigated crops

ai.seo_question: What is the zakat rate for raisins, dates, and grain crops in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records Sama'a ibn Mihran's question to the Imam (likely Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him) about the zakat threshold and rate for raisins, dates, and grain crops. The Imam specifies the nisab (minimum threshold) for raisins and dates as five awsaq (one wasq = sixty sa'as), and distinguishes two rates for grain crops: a full tenth for rain-irrigated land and a half-tenth for land irrigated by human effort such as buckets and water-wheels. This distinction reflects the principle that greater human labor reduces the zakat obligation, a ruling consistent with the broader Shia jurisprudential tradition.
